quiz.title: Which permit do you need?
quiz.intro: Answer four questions. This follows Texas law (Human Resources Code, Chapter 42). HHSC makes the final decision.
quiz.location: Where will you care for children?
quiz.unrelated: At the same time, how many children who are not related to you?
quiz.deed: Do your neighborhood's deed restrictions ban home businesses?

outcomes.related_only: Caring only for your own relatives does not need a permit from HHSC.
outcomes.unpaid_small: Texas requires listing when you are paid to care for 3 or fewer unrelated children. If you won't be paid, you may not need a permit. Confirm with HHSC.
outcomes.listed: You likely need a listed family home. Steps are below.
outcomes.registered: You likely need a registered child-care home. Steps are below.
outcomes.licensed_home: You likely need a licensed child-care home (called a group day-care home in state law). Steps are below.
outcomes.center: Care for 7 or more children away from your home is a day-care center, which needs a center license. This guide covers home daycares only.
outcomes.too_many_for_home: Texas home permits allow no more than 12 children at a time. For more, you would need a day-care center license.
outcomes.center_small: State law defines a day-care center as 7 or more children away from home. For fewer children in another building, ask HHSC which permit applies.

quiz.deedBlocker: Stop here first: if your deed restrictions ban home businesses, you could be forced to close even after you get a state permit. Talk to your civic club or a lawyer before spending money.
quiz.deedCheck: Check your deed restrictions before you spend money. Houston has no zoning, but deed restrictions can legally ban home businesses.

need.title: Where Houston needs more childcare
need.intro: Licensed seats compared with young children whose parents all work, by ZIP code area in Harris County.
need.deserts: {n} of {total} ZIP areas are childcare deserts
need.desertDef: A childcare desert has more than 3 children under 6 with working parents for every licensed seat (fewer than 33.3 seats per 100 children).
need.multi: Crosses a county line: part of this area is outside Harris County.
need.afro: Afro-Latino residents (Hispanic and Black) in these areas: about {n}, margin of error ±{moe}.
need.m1: Licensed seats: total licensed capacity of active centers and homes in Texas HHSC licensing data. Capacity is not the same as open seats, and it includes school-age seats.
need.m2: Children: Census American Community Survey table B23008, children under 6 living with parents who are all in the labor force.
need.m3: ZIP areas are Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, which closely match but are not identical to postal ZIP codes.
need.m4: Children at Risk uses the same 3-to-1 definition. Their method may differ in details, so their list and ours may not match exactly.
need.empty: Need data is not loaded yet. Run the data pipeline first.
